newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Macquarie dips on div credits crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Macquarie dips on div credits crackdown.

text.p: Shares in investment house Macquarie Bank Ltd lost nearly three percent to an intraday low of A$9.28 on Wednesday as traders assessed the impact of the Federal government's crackdown on trade in franking credits.
The Federal Government said in its 1997/98 budget on Tuesday that it would act on dividend washing and dividend streaming to protect the tax base.

Arrangements that allowed franking credits to be transferred by separating legal ownership from the economic risks of share ownership undermined the principles under which the franking credits law was created, the government said.
Traders said that through its stockbroking arm Macquarie was a major player in franking credits trade and stood to lose business as the government implemented its new measures.
"It is generally thought Macquarie is going to be hardest hit by it," said a Sydney trader.
"They have a huge business on that side of things."

Other institutional brokers are also very active in franking credits trading but are not listed on the Australian Stock Exchange. By 1.15 p.m. (0315 GMT), Macquarie shares were 19 cents lower at A$9.35 on turnover of 147,585 shares.
